title: Microsoft Purview: protect data sent to unmanaged cloud apps through Palo Alto Prisma Access
summary: The briefing passes: the current Microsoft documentation supports the opt-in default, licensing, network controls and limits, and the rollout dates match Microsoft's records. Minor corrections are needed to expand abbreviated policy routes, acknowledge differing request definitions and stop pointing to policy creation as the control for rule actions.

claims.claim: The network DLP policy route uses the documented Inline web traffic and Custom policy choices and reaches Network and non-Microsoft secure browsers.
claims.quote: Select Inline web traffic. Select Custom from the Categories list and then select Custom policy from the Regulations list. ... On the Choose where to enforce the policy page, ensure Network and non-Microsoft secure browsers is On
claims.fix: Expand controls[1].ui.path and its rendered copy to 'Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Inline web traffic > Custom > Custom policy > + Add cloud apps > Adaptive app scopes > All unmanaged AI apps > Edit scope > Include only specific > + Add inclusions > Specific users and groups > group > Choose where to enforce the policy > Network and non-Microsoft secure browsers'. The omitted intermediate choices select the apps and users the policy applies to; the printed steps are in the documented order.

claims.claim: New-DlpCompliancePolicy -Name <policy name> -EnforcementPlanes @("Network") creates a network DLP policy using documented parameters and value.
claims.quote: Use the New-DlpCompliancePolicy cmdlet to create data loss prevention (DLP) policies ... The EnforcementPlanes parameter defines the layer where policy actions are run. ... -EnforcementPlanes @("<Value>"). Valid values are: ... Network

claims.claim: The collection-policy route uses documented labels in order and reaches network detection, while abbreviating classifier and target selections.
claims.quote: Open the Data loss prevention solution and navigate to Classifiers > Collection policies. ... Select Classifiers and then Edit. ... Select + Add activities. ... Select the Unmanaged cloud apps tab. ... Ensure Network and non-Microsoft secure browsers is enabled
claims.fix: Expand controls[2].ui.path and its rendered copy to 'Data loss prevention > Classifiers > Collection policies > + Create policy > + Add condition > Content contains > Classifiers > Edit > Scope for classifiers > Exclude classifiers > + Exclude classifiers > Choose Classifiers > classifiers > + Add activities > activities > + Add data source > Unmanaged cloud apps > apps > Edit scope > Include only specific > Included > + Add inclusions > group > Don't capture content > Network and non-Microsoft secure browsers'. This spells out the cited scenario's classifier and policy-target selections and default content-capture choice.
